newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank sector still snagged by sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German bank sector still snagged by sick pay.

text.p: New talks between Germany's banking employers and the main trade unions in the sector over threatened cuts to sick pay were called off after only a few hours on Monday as no scope for agreement was found.
At issue is a 20 percent cut in German sick pay entitlements made possible by a new law introduced late last year and which German banks had initially implemented.
However, following mass worker protests the banks later backed down, saying they would seek to gain a definitive agreement on the issue with negotiators from the two trade unions in the sector.
The breakdown of the third and latest set of talks now means that the dispute will be handled within the regular wage round on the sector, which is due to start on April 17.

The failure to reach an agreement over sick pay heightens the possibility of increased industrial action. Under existing work contracts, the 450,000 employees in the sector could begin to organise strikes from May onwards.
Union and employer negotiators said talks broke down due to disagreement on the extent of compensatory cost-cutting measures employers could demand if they agreed to keep sick pay intact.
